import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Teaching Content
        title = "Introducing the Triangle of Power"
        lines = [
            "Meet the Triangle of Power, a unified geometric map.",
            "Place the Base at the bottom-left vertex.",
            "The Exponent sits naturally at the very top.",
            "Finally, the Result occupies the bottom-right corner.",
            "One shape now replaces all three traditional notations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_BASE = "#3498DB"
        COLOR_EXP = "#E74C3C"
        COLOR_RES = "#2ECC71"
        
        # Define base triangle coordinates
        pos_base_vertex = self.grid["E2"]
        pos_res_vertex = self.grid["E5"]
        # Top vertex is exactly between B3 and B4 for horizontal centering
        pos_exp_vertex = (self.grid["B3"] + self.grid["B4"]) / 2
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Meet the Triangle of Power, a unified geometric map.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        triangle = Polygon(
            pos_base_vertex, 
            pos_res_vertex, 
            pos_exp_vertex, 
            color=WHITE, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        self.play(Create(triangle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Place the Base at the bottom-left vertex.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASE))
        # Label centered under the vertex
        base_label = MathTex("\\text{Base}", color=COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_in_area(base_label, "F1", "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(base_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The Exponent sits naturally at the very top.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_EXP))
        # Label centered above the vertex
        exp_label = MathTex("\\text{Exponent}", color=COLOR_EXP)
        self.place_in_area(exp_label, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(exp_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Finally, the Result occupies the bottom-right corner.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_RES))
        # Label centered under the vertex
        res_label = MathTex("\\text{Result}", color=COLOR_RES)
        self.place_in_area(res_label, "F4", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(res_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # One shape now replaces all three traditional notations.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Connections using arrows following the descriptions
        # Curved arrows for sides, straight for bottom
        # angle=-PI/4 for outward curves
        arrow_be = CurvedArrow(pos_base_vertex, pos_exp_vertex, angle=-PI/4, color=WHITE, tip_length=0.2)
        arrow_er = CurvedArrow(pos_exp_vertex, pos_res_vertex, angle=-PI/4, color=WHITE, tip_length=0.2)
        # Horizontal arrow at bottom
        arrow_br = Arrow(pos_base_vertex, pos_res_vertex, color=WHITE, buff=0.1, tip_length=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Create(arrow_be),
            Create(arrow_er),
            Create(arrow_br),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and outline
        title = "Operation 1: Calculating the Power"
        lecture_lines = [
            "To find a power, look at the bottom right.",
            "The Base 'climbing' the Exponent produces the Result.",
            "Five squared yields twenty-five in our triangle."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_l1 = "#F39C12" # Orange
        color_l2 = "#3498DB" # Blue
        color_l3 = "#2ECC71" # Green (Matches the #2ECC71 requirement)
        
        # Vertices for the Triangle of Power (Visual Area: Col 2 to 6)
        # Choosing E2, C3, E4 to stay well away from lecture text (Col 1)
        p_base = self.grid["E2"]
        p_exp = self.grid["C3"]
        p_res = self.grid["E4"]
        
        triangle = Polygon(p_base, p_exp, p_res, color=WHITE, stroke_width=3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "To find a power, look at the bottom right."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_l1))
        
        # Initial labels at vertices
        label_base = MathTex("\\text{Base}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_base, "E2", scale_factor=0.6).shift(LEFT * 0.6 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        label_exp = MathTex("\\text{Exponent}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_exp, "C3", scale_factor=0.6).shift(UP * 0.5)
        
        res_q = MathTex("?", color=color_l1)
        self.place_at_grid(res_q, "E4", scale_factor=1.2).shift(RIGHT * 0.6 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle))
        self.play(Write(label_base), Write(label_exp), Write(res_q))
        self.play(Flash(res_q, color=color_l1, flash_radius=0.4))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The Base 'climbing' the Exponent produces the Result."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_l2))
        
        # Bold/Highlight Base and Exponent
        self.play(
            label_base.animate.set_color(color_l2).scale(1.1),
            label_exp.animate.set_color(color_l2).scale(1.1)
        )
        
        # Visualizing "climbing" path
        climb_arrow = Arrow(p_base, p_exp, color=color_l2, buff=0.1, stroke_width=4)
        result_arrow = Arrow(p_exp, p_res, color=color_l2, buff=0.1, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(climb_arrow))
        self.play(GrowArrow(result_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Five squared yields twenty-five in our triangle."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_l3))
        
        # Prepare final values (Script uses 5^2 = 25)
        val_5 = MathTex("5", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(val_5, "E2", scale_factor=0.8).shift(LEFT * 0.6 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        val_2 = MathTex("2", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(val_2, "C3", scale_factor=0.8).shift(UP * 0.5)
        
        # Note: Script says 25, so we use 25 in color #2ECC71
        val_25 = MathTex("25", color=color_l3)
        self.place_at_grid(val_25, "E4", scale_factor=1.1).shift(RIGHT * 0.6 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(label_base, val_5),
            Transform(label_exp, val_2),
            Transform(res_q, val_25),
            triangle.animate.set_color(color_l3),
            FadeOut(climb_arrow),
            FadeOut(result_arrow)
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(res_q, color=color_l3, scale_factor=1.4))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "Operation 2: Finding the Root"
        lecture_lines = [
            "To find a root, look at the bottom left.",
            "We seek the foundation for this exponent and result.",
            "The cube root of twenty-seven reveals the base three."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors for the Triangle of Power components
        COLOR_EXP = "#F1C40F"  # Yellow for Exponent
        COLOR_RES = "#E67E22"  # Orange for Result
        COLOR_BASE = "#3498DB" # Blue for Base (Root)
        
        # Position vertices of the triangle on the right side of the screen
        # Using columns 4, 5, 6 to respect Belief B021 (gap from lecture text)
        v_top_pos = "B5"
        v_left_pos = "E4"
        v_right_pos = "E6"
        
        v_top = self.grid[v_top_pos]
        v_left = self.grid[v_left_pos]
        v_right = self.grid[v_right_pos]
        
        # The Triangle visual
        triangle = Polygon(v_top, v_right, v_left, color=WHITE, stroke_width=3)
        
        # Prepare Mobjects (positioned at grid points near vertices)
        # Exponent label at A5 (above top vertex B5)
        exponent = MathTex("3", color=COLOR_EXP)
        self.place_at_grid(exponent, "A5", scale_factor=1.4)
        
        # Result label at F6 (below bottom-right vertex E6)
        result = MathTex("27", color=COLOR_RES)
        self.place_at_grid(result, "F6", scale_factor=1.4)
        
        # Base/Root question mark at F4 (below bottom-left vertex E4)
        base_q = MathTex("?", color=COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(base_q, "F4", scale_factor=1.6)
        
        # Final Base value at the same position
        base_val = MathTex("3", color=COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(base_val, "F4", scale_factor=1.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: "To find a root, look at the bottom left."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASE))
        self.play(Create(triangle), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(exponent), FadeIn(result))
        
        # Animation: Bold the Exponent and Result values to show they are known.
        self.play(
            exponent.animate.scale(1.2).set_stroke(width=1.5),
            result.animate.scale(1.2).set_stroke(width=1.5),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: "We seek the foundation for this exponent and result."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASE))
        
        # Animation: Show a flashing "?" at the Base vertex (bottom left area).
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(FadeIn(base_q, run_time=0.25))
            self.play(FadeOut(base_q, run_time=0.25))
        self.play(FadeIn(base_q))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: "The cube root of twenty-seven reveals the base three."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASE))
        
        # Animation: Transform the "?" into the number "3" (Corrected from storyboard typo '2')
        # Also return the Exponent and Result to their normal scale/weight.
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(base_q, base_val),
            exponent.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_stroke(width=0),
            result.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_stroke(width=0),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Unified Summary"
        lines = [
            "- All three operations live within this single triangle.",
            "- Rotating our focus reveals powers, roots, or logs.",
            "- The numbers two, three, and eight never move.",
            "- One consistent map for all exponential math.",
            "- Mathematics becomes simpler when we see the connections."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Define colors for lecture lines
        line_colors = [BLUE_B, GREEN_B, YELLOW_B, GOLD_B, PURPLE_B]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(line_colors[0]))
        
        # Vertices positions: Bottom-Left (D2), Top (B3), Bottom-Right (D4)
        v_base_pos = self.grid["D2"]
        v_exp_pos = self.grid["B3"]
        v_pow_pos = self.grid["D4"]
        
        triangle = Polygon(v_base_pos, v_exp_pos, v_pow_pos, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Vertex Values
        val_base = MathTex("2", color=BLUE_B)
        val_exp = MathTex("3", color=GREEN_B)
        val_pow = MathTex("8", color=RED_B)
        
        self.place_at_grid(val_base, "D2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(val_exp, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(val_pow, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle), Write(val_base), Write(val_exp), Write(val_pow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(line_colors[1])
        )
        
        # Operations labels
        label_power = MathTex("2^3 = 8", font_size=24, color=YELLOW_B)
        self.place_at_grid(label_power, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        label_root = MathTex(r"\sqrt[3]{8} = 2", font_size=24, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_root, "C1", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        label_log = MathTex(r"\log_2(8) = 3", font_size=24, color=PURPLE_B)
        self.place_at_grid(label_log, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pulse edges
        self.play(triangle.animate.set_stroke(width=8, color=GREEN_B), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(triangle.animate.set_stroke(width=4, color=WHITE), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label_power), FadeIn(label_root), FadeIn(label_log))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(line_colors[2])
        )
        
        # Highlight symmetry by rotating slightly
        tri_group = VGroup(triangle, val_base, val_exp, val_pow, label_power, label_root, label_log)
        center_point = tri_group.get_center()
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(tri_group, angle=15*DEGREES, about_point=center_point),
            run_time=0.8,
            rate_func=wiggle
        )
        
        # Pulse the numbers
        self.play(
            Indicate(val_base, color=BLUE_B),
            Indicate(val_exp, color=GREEN_B),
            Indicate(val_pow, color=RED_B)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(line_colors[3])
        )
        
        # Scale to fill the frame
        # Transform the core triangle and numbers to a larger size in the area
        core_group = VGroup(triangle, val_base, val_exp, val_pow)
        large_group = core_group.copy()
        self.place_in_area(large_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=2.0)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(core_group, large_group),
            FadeOut(label_power), FadeOut(label_root), FadeOut(label_log)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(line_colors[4])
        )
        
        # Final indication and fade out
        self.play(Indicate(large_group, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(large_group),
            FadeOut(self.lecture),
            FadeOut(self.title)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Triangle of Power: A Unified Notation for Powers, Roots, and Logarithms
outline.target_audience: High school students and math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Mathematical Fragmentations
sections.content: Introduce the problem: Traditional notation uses three completely different symbols (superscripts, radical signs, and 'log' abbreviations) to describe the same relationship between three numbers. Use an animation of a character, 'Leo the Architect', trying to build a bridge using three different manual types that don't match.
sections.example: Show 2³ = 8, ∛8 = 2, and log₂(8) = 3. Highlight how the numbers 2, 3, and 8 move positions confusingly in each format.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Three Roles
sections.content: Define the three components of any exponential relationship: The Base (the multiplier), the Exponent (the count), and the Result (the product). Use a 'Magnifying Glass' visual to identify these roles in a simple expression.
sections.example: In 2³ = 8, 2 is the 'Base' (The Root), 3 is the 'Exponent' (The Growth), and 8 is the 'Result' (The Value).

sections.title: Introducing the Triangle of Power
sections.content: Present a single geometric shape: An equilateral triangle. Map the roles to the vertices: Base at the bottom-left, Exponent at the top, and Result at the bottom-right. Explain that this single diagram replaces all three traditional notations.
sections.example: A glowing triangle appears. The number 2 sits at the bottom-left, 3 at the top, and 8 at the bottom-right. Lines connect them to show their interdependence.

sections.title: Operation 1: Calculating the Power
sections.content: When the bottom-left (Base) and top (Exponent) are known, we calculate the bottom-right (Result). In the triangle, this is visualized as the base 'climbing' to the exponent to produce the result.
sections.example: If the bottom-left is 5 and the top is 2, the bottom-right vertex pulses with a question mark until it transforms into 25 (5² = 25).

sections.title: Operation 2: Finding the Root
sections.content: When the top (Exponent) and bottom-right (Result) are known, we find the bottom-left (Base). This is the 'Root' operation. Visually, we are looking for the 'foundation' of the triangle.
sections.example: A triangle shows 3 at the top and 27 at the bottom-right. To find the bottom-left, we calculate the 3rd root of 27. The vertex fills in with 3.

sections.title: Operation 3: Solving the Logarithm
sections.content: When both bottom corners (Base and Result) are known, we find the top (Exponent). This is the 'Logarithm'. Visually, we are asking: 'To what height must the base be raised to reach this result?'
sections.example: A triangle shows 10 at the bottom-left and 1000 at the bottom-right. The top vertex is empty. The calculation reveals 3, because 10³ = 1000 (log₁₀ 1000 = 3).

sections.title: The Unified Summary
sections.content: Show all three operations happening on the same triangle simultaneously. Explain that by rotating our focus around the triangle, we transition between powers, roots, and logs without changing the underlying 'map' of the numbers.
sections.example: An animation shows Leo the Architect spinning a single triangle. As it rotates, it highlights different corners, showing how '2, 3, 8' always stay in their specific vertices regardless of which one is the 'unknown' x.
